_comment: safety 大类自写批 · helicone 正文英译（2026-11-21，Apache-2.0 与云端/自托管口径已核）。axes 八维、runs/unknowns 对应「官方口径与未核到项 / 未知项清单」；related/sources 按索引对齐。

axes.model_access: The official AI Gateway docs describe an open-source Rust router exposing one OpenAI-compatible interface to 100+ language models, with provider keys centralised in the gateway; both cloud-hosted and self-hosted forms are listed. It is not a model provider.
axes.runtime: The cloud-hosted gateway runs on the platform, with an official 99.9% SLA and global edge network. The self-hosted gateway ships as one lightweight Rust binary for Docker, Kubernetes, bare-metal or sidecar use; the full observability stack can run via Docker Compose or Helm.
axes.local_files: In cloud form, requests and logs live on Helicone's side. In self-hosted form, Web, Jawn, Supabase, ClickHouse and Minio run on your own infrastructure, so logs and object storage stay under your control. The gateway itself does not run local models.
axes.background: The gateway sits in the request path and forwards or falls back per call. The official material does not list a durable task queue as a product surface; background jobs are left to the caller's orchestration. Log writes are part of the cloud or self-hosted stack.
axes.tools: The docs list integrations including the OpenAI SDK, Anthropic, LangChain, Gemini and Vercel AI SDK. The gateway provides OpenAI-compatible syntax, caching, rate limits, fallbacks and built-in tracing. An MCP server is not part of the AI Gateway capability surface as documented.
axes.context: The gateway keeps no conversation memory: context is the request body, and length belongs to the upstream model. The observability layer stores traces and sessions for debugging, but the docs do not feed historical traces back as model context.
axes.permissions: Cloud use centralises keys and spend controls in the account; self-hosting leaves key and data permissions to your deployment. Team tiers, audit logs and export details are not itemised in the official docs.
axes.fit: Fits: teams standardising several model providers with fallback, caching, rate limits and observability, or teams that need data inside their own infrastructure and will run the self-hosted gateway. Does not fit: those expecting the gateway to supply model capability, or those unwilling to operate ClickHouse, Minio and Supabase dependencies.

runs: No measured runs on latency, availability or failover conditions. "100+ models", "99.9% SLA" and "within seconds" are quoted from official pages; the site does not treat those figures as evidence for a ranking, and draws no comparison against similar products. Licence and self-hosting statements come from the official Open Source and AI Gateway Introduction pages.
unknowns:
- Exact retention period and deletion UI for cloud request/response logs (not itemised in the official docs)
- Whether logged data is used for training or product improvement
- Team permission tiers, audit logs and export details
- Billing and quota terms (prices are not recorded in entries)
- Capacity planning and upgrade paths for the self-hosted stack (check the deployment docs)
